```{r}

# START of THE ANALYSIS AND PLOTS FOR THE PAPER.

# Figure 1: Map of identified SAMHE sites and corresponding DEFRA sites.
# • Objective: RQ1 / Objective 1 (describes network and pairing quality).
# • Stats: Descriptive only – calculate mean, median, range and distribution of SAMHE–AURN distances. 

# PLESE NOTE: This code chunk is for visualisation purposes only and does not perform any statistical analysis. It creates a map showing the locations of the SAMHE sites and their paired AURN sites, with lines connecting each pair and coloured by distance.

pacman::p_load(dplyr, sf, ggplot2, rnaturalearth)

# ---- 1. Prepare pairing table ----
pairs <- In_Out_24 %>%
  distinct(SchoolId_short, site, .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
  select(
    SchoolId_short,
    SAMHE_lon = SchoolLongitude,
    SAMHE_lat = SchoolLatitude,
    AURN_site = site,
    AURN_lon  = longitude,
    AURN_lat  = latitude,
    distance_km = km_distance_to_AURN
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(SAMHE_lat), !is.na(AURN_lat), !is.na(distance_km)) 

# ---- 2. Descriptive statistics label ----
dist_stats <- pairs %>%
  summarise(
    n_schools = n_distinct(SchoolId_short),
    mean_km   = mean(distance_km, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_km = median(distance_km, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_km    = min(distance_km, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_km    = max(distance_km, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

stats_label <- paste0(
  "n = ", dist_stats$n_schools, "\n",
  "Mean = ", round(dist_stats$mean_km, 1), " km\n",
  "Median = ", round(dist_stats$median_km, 1), " km\n",
  "Range = ", round(dist_stats$min_km, 1), "–", round(dist_stats$max_km, 0), " km"
)

# ---- 3. Convert to sf objects ----
samhe_sf <- st_as_sf(pairs, coords = c("SAMHE_lon", "SAMHE_lat"),
                     crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) 

aurn_sf  <- st_as_sf(pairs, coords = c("AURN_lon", "AURN_lat"),
                     crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

lines_sf <- st_as_sf(
  pairs %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(geometry = st_sfc(
      st_linestring(matrix(c(SAMHE_lon, SAMHE_lat,
                             AURN_lon,  AURN_lat),
                           ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE)),
      crs = 4326)) %>%
    ungroup(),
  crs = 4326 
)

# ---- 4. UK basemap ----
uk <- rnaturalearth::ne_states(country = "United Kingdom", returnclass = "sf") 

# ---- 5. Plot ----
ggplot() +
  # slightly darker basemap so points pop
  geom_sf(data = uk, fill = "grey95", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3) +

  # keep link lines subtle (optional)
  geom_sf(data = lines_sf, colour = "grey65", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.5) +

  # AURN sites as hollow circles
  geom_sf(data = aurn_sf, shape = 21, fill = "white", colour = "black",
          size = 1.0, stroke = 0.3) + 

  # SAMHE sites coloured by distance (high contrast)
  #geom_sf(data = samhe_sf,
          #aes(color = distance_km),
          #shape = 16,#
          #size = 1.0) +
  # add an outline by drawing the points twice: black underneath, coloured on top

geom_sf(data = samhe_sf, colour = "black", shape = 16, size = 1.5, alpha = 0.5) +
geom_sf(data = samhe_sf, aes(color = distance_km), shape = 16, size = 1.3, alpha = 0.5) +

  coord_sf(xlim = c(-8.5, 2.5),
           ylim = c(49.5, 60.9),
           clip = "off") + 
  
scale_color_viridis_c(
  trans = "log10",
  option = "viridis",
  breaks = c(1, 10, 100),
  labels = c("1", "10", "100 km"),
  name = "Distance to nearest AURN"
) +
  # high-contrast distance palette
  #scale_color_distiller(
 #   palette = "RdYlGn", 
 #   direction = -1,
 #   trans = "log10",
 #    breaks = c(1, 10, 100),
 # labels = c("1", "10", "100 km"),
 # name = "Distance to nearest AURN (km)"
#) +

  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = c(1.1, 0.8),
    legend.justification = c(1, 0.5),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.text  = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.margin = margin(5.5, 95, 5.5, 5.5)
  ) +

  # stats block in right margin under legend
  annotate("text",
           x = 0.5,
           y = 57.4,
           label = stats_label,
           hjust = 0,
           vjust = 1,
           size = 3.5)+
# blue dot

 annotate("point",
         x = 0.65,
         y = 57.8,
         shape = 21,
         colour = "black",
         fill = "white",
         size = 1.5,
         stroke = 0.5) +
         
# label next to dot
 annotate("text",
         x = 0.8,
         y = 57.8,
         label = "  AURN sites",
         hjust = 0,
         size = 3.5)
```

```{r}

# this plot is for visualisation purposes only and does not perform any statistical analysis. It creates a time series plot showing the daily mean indoor and outdoor PM2.5 levels, with shaded ribbons representing the interquartile range (25th to 75th percentile) for each site. The correlation coefficient (R²) is annotated on the plot.

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2) 
library(openair) 
library(ggpubr) # for stat_cor() function

# daily is a long format dataset, i did check the r, r2 and p values using the wide format dataset "wide_daily" and the cor() and cor.test() functions, and they match the values from the modStats() function, so I am confident that the correlation is being calculated correctly. (it was) 

daily <- In_Out_24 %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(DateTime)) %>%
  group_by(date) %>% # group by date to calculate daily statistics across all schools for each day
  summarise(
    Indoor_mean   = mean(pm02, na.rm = TRUE),
    Indoor_q25    = quantile(pm02, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Indoor_q75    = quantile(pm02, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    Outdoor_mean  = mean(pm2.5, na.rm = TRUE),
    Outdoor_q25   = quantile(pm2.5, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    Outdoor_q75   = quantile(pm2.5, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = -date,
    names_to = c("site", ".value"),
    names_pattern = "(Indoor|Outdoor)_(mean|q25|q75)"
  )

r <- cor(daily$mean[daily$site == "Indoor"],
         daily$mean[daily$site == "Outdoor"],
         use = "complete.obs")
r2_spearman <- cor(
  daily$mean[daily$site == "Indoor"],
  daily$mean[daily$site == "Outdoor"],
  method = "spearman",
  use = "complete.obs"
)^2

p <- cor.test(
  daily$mean[daily$site == "Indoor"],
  daily$mean[daily$site == "Outdoor"]
)$p.value

ggplot(daily, aes(x = date, y = mean, colour = site, fill = site)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75),
              alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.25) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(Outdoor = "#E57200", Indoor = "#7A1FA2"),
    labels = c(Outdoor = "Outdoor (DEFRA)", Indoor = "Indoor (SAMHE)")
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(Outdoor = "#E57200", Indoor = "#7A1FA2"),
    labels = c(Outdoor = "Outdoor (DEFRA)", Indoor = "Indoor (SAMHE)")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Date",
    y = expression("Daily mean PM"[2.5]),
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = min(daily$date),
    y = max(daily$mean),
    label = paste0 ("R² = ", round(r2_spearman, 2), ", p < 0.001"),
    hjust = 0
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    aspect.ratio = 0.25
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%b '%y")

ggsave("plot.png", width = 24, height = 4, dpi = 300)

```




```{r}

# Figure 2: Scatter plot of annual mean indoor PM2.5 on the y-axis and annual mean outdoor
# PM2.5 on the x-axis.
# • Objective: RQ1 / Objective 1 (baseline exposure and infiltration).
# • Stats: Pearson (or Spearman if non-normal) correlation between indoor and outdoor PM₂.₅.
# • Simple linear regression: indoor PM₂.₅ ~ outdoor PM₂.₅

pacman::p_load(dplyr, openair, tidyverse)

# this code uses the whole timeset and not for term and occupancy time; that is plotted on the next plot!

# ---- ALL TIME (24-hour) ----
df_annual_all <- In_Out_24 %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(format(DateTime, "%Y"))) %>%
  filter(Year %in% 2023:2025) %>%
  group_by(SchoolId_short) %>%
  summarise(
    indoor_pm25  = mean(pm02, na.rm = TRUE),
    outdoor_pm25 = mean(pm2.5, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(indoor_pm25), !is.na(outdoor_pm25))

r_all  <- cor(df_annual_all$outdoor_pm25, df_annual_all$indoor_pm25)
r2_all <- r_all^2
p_all  <- cor.test(df_annual_all$outdoor_pm25,
                   df_annual_all$indoor_pm25)$p.value

scatterPlot(
  df_annual_all,
  x = "outdoor_pm25",
  y = "indoor_pm25",
  linear = TRUE,
  cor = TRUE,
  xlim = c(0, 20),
  ylim = c(0, 20),
  aspect = 1,
  main = "2023:2025 Indoor vs Outdoor PM2.5 (All time)"
)

```

```{r}

# Figure 3: I/O annual mean scatterplot (faceted 2023-24 2024-25), different colours for school region, etc?)
#• RQ / Objective: RQ1 / Objective 1 (infiltration behaviour and its variability).
#• Stats: Pearson/Spearman correlation between I/O ratio and outdoor PM₂.₅.
#• Optionally compare I/O distributions by region (ANOVA or Kruskal–Wallis, depending on normality).

library(dplyr)
library(openair)

# Annual means per school (2023:2025) + I/O ratio. each school is plotted per year so three dots per school, and the regression line is fitted across all schools and years. I/O ratio is plotted against outdoor PM2.5 to show how infiltration varies with outdoor concentration, which is a key question for the paper.

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Create annual school-year means and I/O ratio
df_annual_io <- In_Out_SchHrs %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(format(DateTime, "%Y"))) %>%
  filter(Year %in% 2023:2025) %>%
  group_by(SchoolId_short, Year) %>%
  summarise(
    indoor_pm25  = mean(pm02, na.rm = TRUE),
    outdoor_pm25 = mean(`pm2.5`, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(indoor_pm25),
    is.finite(outdoor_pm25),
    outdoor_pm25 > 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(io_ratio = indoor_pm25 / outdoor_pm25)

# 2. Plotting dataframe
df_plot <- df_annual_io %>%
  filter(io_ratio > 0) %>%
  mutate(Year = factor(Year))

# 3. Statistics
cor_test <- cor.test(df_plot$outdoor_pm25, df_plot$io_ratio, method = "pearson")
lm_fit   <- lm(io_ratio ~ outdoor_pm25, data = df_plot)

r_val  <- unname(cor_test$estimate)
p_val  <- cor_test$p.value
r2_val <- summary(lm_fit)$r.squared
n_val  <- nrow(df_plot)

stats_label <- paste0(
  "n = ", n_val,
  "\nPearson r = ", round(r_val, 2),
  "\np = ", format.pval(p_val, digits = 2, eps = .001),
  "\nR² = ", round(r2_val, 2)
)

# 4. Plot
ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = outdoor_pm25, y = io_ratio, colour = Year)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "black") +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = Inf, y = Inf,
    label = stats_label,
    hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.2,
    size = 5
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 2)) +
  labs(
    x = "Annual mean outdoor PM2.5 (µg m-3)",
    y = "Annual mean I/O ratio",
    colour = "Year",
    title = "Annual mean I/O ratio vs outdoor PM2.5 (2023–2025)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

```

```{r}
# Figure 4: Indoor PM2.5 vs ventilation type boxplot (different ventilation types)
# • RQ / Objective: RQ3 / Objective 3 (building-level determinants).
# • Stats: Group comparison of indoor PM₂.₅ across ventilation types: ANOVA (if normal) or Kruskal–Wallis (if non-normal). Post-hoc pairwise tests if significant.

pacman::p_load(dplyr, ggplot2)

df_plot <- In_Out_SchHrs %>%
  group_by(SchoolId_short) %>%
  summarise(
    indoor_pm25 = mean(pm02, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    df_school_chars %>%
      select(SchoolId_short, BuildingEnvironment) %>%
      distinct(),
    by = "SchoolId_short"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(BuildingEnvironment), !is.na(indoor_pm25))

anova_mod <- aov(indoor_pm25 ~ BuildingEnvironment, data = df_plot)
anova_tab <- summary(anova_mod)[[1]]
f_val <- round(anova_tab$`F value`[1], 2)
p_val <- signif(anova_tab$`Pr(>F)`[1], 2)

n_df <- df_plot %>%
  count(BuildingEnvironment)

y_max <- max(df_plot$indoor_pm25, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = BuildingEnvironment, y = indoor_pm25)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_text(
    data = n_df,
    aes(x = BuildingEnvironment, y = y_max * 1.03, label = paste0("n=", n)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 1,
    y = y_max * 1.12,
    hjust = 0,
    label = paste0("ANOVA: F = ", f_val, ", p = ", p_val),
    size = 4
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Ventilation type",
    y = expression("Annual mean indoor PM"[2.5]~"(µg/m"^3*")")
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

summary(anova_mod)

```
```{r}

# the above plot compares indoor PM2.5 across all the different building environment categories, which is a bit messy and hard to interpret, so here I have grouped the categories into "Mechanical" (heating & mechanical ventilation + air conditioning) vs "Natural" (heating & natural ventilation), which is a more meaningful comparison for the paper and easier to interpret. The ANOVA is still performed on the original categories, but the boxplot is shown for the grouped categories.


pacman::p_load(dplyr, ggplot2)

df_plot <- In_Out_SchHrs %>%
  group_by(SchoolId_short) %>%
  summarise(
    indoor_pm25 = mean(pm02, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    df_school_chars %>%
      select(SchoolId_short, BuildingEnvironment) %>%
      distinct(),
    by = "SchoolId_short"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(BuildingEnvironment), !is.na(indoor_pm25)) %>%
  mutate(
    Vent_group = case_when(
      BuildingEnvironment %in% c("Heating and Mechanical Ventilation", "Air Conditioning") ~ "Mechanical",
      BuildingEnvironment == "Heating and Natural Ventilation" ~ "Natural",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Vent_group))

tt <- t.test(indoor_pm25 ~ Vent_group, data = df_plot)
p_val <- signif(tt$p.value, 2)

n_df <- df_plot %>% count(Vent_group)

y_max <- max(df_plot$indoor_pm25, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = Vent_group, y = indoor_pm25)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_text(
    data = n_df,
    aes(x = Vent_group, y = y_max * 1.03, label = paste0("n=", n)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 1,
    y = y_max * 1.12,
    hjust = 0,
    label = paste0(
      "t-test p = ", p_val, "\n",
      "Mechanical = Heating & Mechanical Ventilation + Air Conditioning\n",
      "Natural = Heating & Natural Ventilation"
    ),
    size = 4
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Ventilation group",
    y = expression("Annual mean indoor PM"[2.5]~"(µg/m"^3*")")
  ) +
  theme_bw()

tt
```











```{r}
# Figure 5: Indoor PM2.5 vs IMD decile (box plot indoor PM2.5 on y-axis, least to most
# deprived on x-axis)
# • RQ / Objective: RQ3 / Objective 3 (socioeconomic context).
# • Stats: Spearman correlation between PM₂.₅ and IMD category.

pacman::p_load(dplyr, ggplot2)

df_plot <- In_Out_SchHrs %>%
  group_by(SchoolId_short) %>%
  summarise(
    indoor_pm25 = mean(pm02, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    df_school_chars %>%
      select(SchoolId_short, IMD_decile) %>%
      distinct(),
    by = "SchoolId_short"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(IMD_decile), !is.na(indoor_pm25)) %>%
  mutate(IMD_decile = factor(IMD_decile, levels = 1:10))

# Spearman
sp <- cor.test(df_plot$indoor_pm25,
               as.numeric(as.character(df_plot$IMD_decile)),
               method = "spearman")

rho <- round(sp$estimate, 2)
pval <- signif(sp$p.value, 2)

# n per decile
n_df <- df_plot %>%
  count(IMD_decile)

ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = IMD_decile, y = indoor_pm25)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, fill = "grey85") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.3, size = 1) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 23, size = 2.5, fill = "black") +
  geom_text(
    data = n_df,
    aes(x = IMD_decile, y = max(df_plot$indoor_pm25, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.05,
        label = paste0("n=", n)),
    size = 3
  ) +
  annotate("text",
           x = 1,
           y = max(df_plot$indoor_pm25, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.15,
           hjust = 0,
           label = paste0("Spearman \u03C1 = ", rho, "\np = ", pval),
           size = 4) +
  labs(
    x = "IMD decile (1 = most deprived, 10 = least deprived)",
    y = expression("Annual mean indoor PM"[2.5]~"(µg/m"^3*")")
  ) +
  theme_bw()


```

```{r}
# Figure 8: CO2 vs I/O PM2.5 ratio scatterplot with non-linear trend line.
# • RQ / Objective: RQ2 / Objective 2 (ventilation interpretation using CO₂).
# • Stats: Spearman correlation between CO₂ and I/O ratio.

pacman::p_load(dplyr, ggplot2)

df_plot <- In_Out_SchHrs %>%
    mutate(Year = as.integer(format(DateTime, "%Y"))) %>%
    group_by(SchoolId_short, Year) %>%
    summarise(
        indoor_pm25  = mean(pm02, na.rm = TRUE),
        outdoor_pm25 = mean(pm2.5, na.rm = TRUE),
        co2          = mean(rco2, na.rm = TRUE),
        io_ratio     = indoor_pm25 / outdoor_pm25,
        .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(io_ratio), !is.na(co2), is.finite(io_ratio)) %>%
    filter(outdoor_pm25 > 1, io_ratio < 5)

# Spearman per year

sp_df <- df_plot %>%
    group_by(Year) %>%
    summarise(
        rho = round(cor(co2, io_ratio, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"), 2),
        p   = signif(cor.test(co2, io_ratio, method = "spearman")$p.value, 2),
        n   = n(),
        .groups = "drop"
    )

y_max <- max(df_plot$io_ratio, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = co2, y = io_ratio, colour = factor(Year))) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
    annotate(
        "text",
        x = min(df_plot$co2, na.rm = TRUE),
        y = y_max,
        hjust = 0,
        label = paste0(
            paste0("Year ", sp_df$Year,
                   ": n=", sp_df$n,
                   ", ρ=", sp_df$rho,
                   ", p=", sp_df$p),
            collapse = "\n"
        )
    ) +
    labs(
        x = "Mean CO2 (ppm)",
        y = "Indoor / Outdoor PM2.5 ratio",
        colour = "Year"
    ) +
    theme_bw()





```


```{r}
# Figure 9: Annual mean I/O PM2.5 ratio by HEPA, Boxplot (with/without filters)
# • RQ / Objective: RQ3 / Objective 3 (effect of HEPA devices).
# • Compare I/O ratios between HEPA vs non-HEPA classrooms using t-test.

pacman::p_load(dplyr, ggplot2)

df_plot <- In_Out_SchHrs %>%
  group_by(SchoolId_short) %>%
  summarise(
    indoor_pm25  = mean(pm02, na.rm = TRUE),
    outdoor_pm25 = mean(pm2.5, na.rm = TRUE),
    io_ratio     = indoor_pm25 / outdoor_pm25,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    df_school_chars %>%
      select(SchoolId_short, MonitoringType) %>%
      distinct(),
    by = "SchoolId_short"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(MonitoringType), !is.na(io_ratio), is.finite(io_ratio)) %>%
  mutate(
    HEPA = case_when(
      MonitoringType == 1 ~ "No HEPA",
      MonitoringType == 2 ~ "HEPA",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(HEPA))

tt <- t.test(io_ratio ~ HEPA, data = df_plot)
p_val <- signif(tt$p.value, 2)

n_df <- df_plot %>%
  count(HEPA)

y_max <- max(df_plot$io_ratio, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = HEPA, y = io_ratio)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_text(
    data = n_df,
    aes(x = HEPA, y = y_max * 1.03, label = paste0("n=", n)),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 3
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 1,
    y = y_max * 1.12,
    hjust = 0,
    label = paste0("t-test p = ", p_val),
    size = 4
  ) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Annual mean indoor / outdoor PM2.5 ratio"
  ) +
  theme_bw() 

tt


```
